question: The purchasing power of money is equal to:
solution:
The correct answer is 1/(Price index number)² 1/Price index number

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **purchasing power of money** refers to the amount of goods or services that can be purchased with a given amount of money.

 
 
• It is a measure of the value of money, and how much it can buy.
 
 
 
• The purchasing power of money is inversely related to the price level in an economy
 
 
• as measured by a price index such as the **Consumer Price Index (CPI) **or the **Producer Price Index (PPI)**.
 
 
 
• When prices are rising, the purchasing power of money decreases, and when prices are falling, the purchasing power of money increases.
 
• The relationship between the purchasing power of money and the price level can be expressed as:
 
 
• Purchasing power = 1/Price index number
 
• So, the purchasing power of money is equal to 1/Price index number.
 
 
 
• This means that the purchasing power of money is directly proportional to the reciprocal of the price index number, which means that as the price index number goes up, the purchasing power of money goes down, and vice versa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The purchasing power of money **is the amount of goods or services that can be purchased with a given amount of money.

 
 
• It is a measure of the value of money and its ability to buy goods and services.
 
• It is inversely related to the price level in an economy, as measured by a price index such as the Consumer Price Index (CPI) or the Producer Price Index (PPI).
 
 
 
• As prices rise, the purchasing power of money decreases, and as prices fall, the purchasing power of money increases.
 
• The purchasing power of money can be expressed as 1/Price index number, which means that it is directly proportional to the reciprocal of the price index number.
 
• Changes in the purchasing power of money can have significant impacts on the economy, such as inflation or deflation, which can affect the cost of living, the demand for goods and services, and the overall level of economic activity.
